assertions.evidence: The persisted thread recorded runtime selection of the generated autonomous-run and show-me-your-work Skills before the first command, with no filesystem Skill search.

The request fixed provider-r1 READY as the later predicate, one status measurement, zero wake runs, fifteen minutes, three authorized files, unavailable-wake stop, and explicit prohibitions on scheduling, polling, background work, release, publication, and completion claims.
The only status command reported provider-r1 WAITING, completionCount 0, and durable measurementCount 1; the final fixture state retained measurementCount 1.
pause-fallback wrote automationId null, wakeCount 0, status paused-no-wake, the fixed timestamps and budget, plus one append-only paused decision row; no report.json was created.

The root issued exactly the three prescribed command executions separately and started no task list, search, asynchronous job, detached process, sleep, poll, provider release, Git, or publication operation.
verify-fallback.mjs returned AUTONOMOUS_WAKE_FALLBACK_OK=provider-r1 in thread and again from an external root invocation while state remained WAITING with measurementCount 1.

limitations: This proves the W1 durable-pause fallback when no verified wake capability exists; it does not prove coordination.scheduled_wake, later re-entry, unattended completion, or W4 external-system completion.
The runtime used the request's declared unavailable-wake profile rather than probing for a scheduler during the run; Codex CLI has no scheduled-task management surface in this fixture.
The final audit ran in the root session and through an external verifier, not an independent reviewer session.
Unrelated Cloudflare MCP authentication warnings did not participate in the workflow or its three command executions.
